'''Howell Peregrine''' (30 December 1938 – 20 March 2007) was a British [[applied mathematician]] noted for his contributions to [[fluid mechanics]], especially of free surface flows such as [[water waves]], and [[coastal engineering]].<ref>{{cite journal| title=Professor D. Howell Peregrine | first=H. K. | last=Moffatt | journal=Journal of Fluid Mechanics | volume=580 | year=2007 | pages=1–2 |bibcode = 2007JFM...580....1M |doi = 10.1017/S0022112007999991 | doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name="Cooker">{{cite journal | title=A commemoration of Howell Peregrine, 30 December 1938–20 March 2007 | author=Cooker, M. | journal=Journal of Engineering Mathematics | year=2010 | volume=67 | issue=1 | pages=1–9 | doi=10.1007/s10665-009-9331-x|bibcode = 2010JEnMa..67....1C | doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite book | editor1-last=Franco | editor1-first=L. | editor2-last=Tomasicchio | editor2-first=G. R. | editor3-last=Lamberti | editor3-first=Alberto | contribution=In memoriam of Howell Peregrine | pages=vii–viii | year=2007 | title=Coastal Structures 2007. Proceedings of the 5th International Conference | publisher=World Scientific | doi=10.1142/9789814282024_fmatter | isbn=978-981-4280-99-0 }}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Howell Peregrine joined the Mathematics Department of [[University of Bristol]] in 1964 following his undergraduate and postgraduate training at [[Oxford University|Oxford]] and [[Cambridge University|Cambridge]].<ref>{{cite web | title = Professor D H Peregrine | publisher= bris.ac.uk | url = http://www.bris.ac.uk/news/2007/5372.html | access-date = 2008-09-20 }}</ref> He spent his entire career at Bristol. One of his most remarkable contributions was the theoretical prediction of a new nonlinear entity, now called the [[Peregrine soliton]],<ref>{{cite journal| title=Water waves, nonlinear Schrödinger equations and their solutions | first=D. H. | last=Peregrine | journal=J. Austral. Math. Soc. |series= B | volume=25 | year=1983 | pages=16–43 |doi= 10.1017/S0334270000003891 | doi-access=free }}</ref> that may explain the formation of hydrodynamics [[rogue wave]]s and that has also been experimentally demonstrated more than 25 years later in the field of [[nonlinear optics|nonlinear fiber optics]]<ref>{{cite journal |last1= Kibler|first1=B. |last2= Fatome |first2= J. | last3= Finot |first3= C. | last4= Millot |first4= G. | last5= Dias |first5= F. | last6= Genty |first6= G. | last7= Akhmediev |first7= N. | last8= Dudley |first8= J.M. | year= 2010 |title= The Peregrine soliton in nonlinear fibre optics|journal= Nature Physics|doi= 10.1038/nphys1740|bibcode = 2010NatPh...6..790K | volume=6 | issue=10 |pages= 790–795|doi-access= free }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title = Peregrine's 'Soliton' observed at last | publisher= bris.ac.uk | url = http://www.bris.ac.uk/news/2010/7184.html | access-date = 2010-08-24 }}</ref> and then in 2011 in hydrodynamics with experiments in a water wave tank.<ref>{{cite journal |last1= Chabchoub|first1=A. |last2= Hoffmann |first2= N.P. | last3= Akhmediev |first3= N. | year= 2011 |title= Rogue wave observation in a water wave tank|journal= Phys. Rev. Lett.|doi= 10.1103/PhysRevLett.106.204502|bibcode = 2011PhRvL.106t4502C |volume= 106 |issue= 20 |pmid=21668234 |article-number=204502|hdl=1885/70717 |s2cid=12444306 |hdl-access= free }}</ref>

He was an [[associate editor]] of the ''[[Journal of Fluid Mechanics]]'' for more than 25 years.

Howell Peregrine died suddenly after a short battle against [[cancer]]. He was at the time a [[emeritus professor|professor emeritus]] of applied mathematics at the University of Bristol.

== Personal ==
Peregrine was known to be a good [[photographer]] of natural phenomena. Some of the photographs which he took himself appeared in his papers.<ref name="Cooker"/>
